16.t: Working with data: red blood cells at altitude
q: Higher up, more red blood cells, and the rise gets steeper.
Explain why this is useful at high altitude.
Air there has less oxygen; more red blood cells (with haemoglobin) can carry more oxygen to the body.
Explain why athletes sometimes train in the mountains before a race at sea level.
Their body makes extra red blood cells. Back at sea level they can carry more oxygen to their muscles for a while, so they tire later.
